# ABI conformance fixtures — *not* generated by V

These two modules are the evidence behind one vcsr claim: **the loader/linker
contract is language-neutral.** vcsr's *frontend* compiles a V component triplet
to WASM, but its *runtime contract* — what a module must export/import and how
DOM handles cross — is defined on the wasm interface, not on V. Any language
that can emit a conforming module (Rust, Zig, C, AssemblyScript, hand-written
WAT) plugs into the same `app.js` loader and is served by the same vanilla
`dist/`.

So these fixtures are deliberately **hand-written WebAssembly text** — the one
form that is obviously not V output:

| File | Role | Contract (see [docs/WASM-ABI.md](../../../docs/WASM-ABI.md)) |
|---|---|---|
| `core.wat` → `core.wasm` | MAIN module | owns + exports `memory`, `__indirect_function_table`, `__v_alloc`, `__v_free`; exports `mount`/`unmount`; DOM crosses as `externref` |
| `route_reports.wat` → `route_reports.wasm` | SIDE module (lazy route) | imports core's `memory`/table/`__memory_base`/`__table_base`/`__v_alloc`; does **not** redefine the allocator; exports `mount`/`unmount`; position-independent |

[`tests/phase_11_abi_conformance_test.v`](../../phase_11_abi_conformance_test.v)
inspects these `.wasm` bytes through vcsr's (not-yet-built) `vcsr.wasm` ABI
reader and asserts the same MAIN/SIDE invariants as
[`phase_07_wasm_linking_test.v`](../../phase_07_wasm_linking_test.v) — but
against modules vcsr *did not produce*. That is the whole point: phase 07 pins
the contract for V output; phase 11 pins that the contract is satisfiable (and
checkable) by **any** producer.

## Recompiling

The `.wasm` files are checked in so the test runs without a toolchain. To
regenerate them you need [WABT](https://github.com/WebAssembly/wabt)'s
`wat2wasm` (reference types are enabled by default since WABT 1.0.30+):

```sh
cd tests/fixtures/abi
wat2wasm core.wat          -o core.wasm
wat2wasm route_reports.wat -o route_reports.wasm
wasm-validate core.wasm route_reports.wasm   # sanity check
```

A real-language equivalent (kept out of the test to avoid a Rust toolchain
dependency) would be, e.g. for the SIDE module:

```rust
// cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown, linked with
// -C link-arg=--relocatable for a SIDE module
#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn mount(root: /* externref */) -> i32 { /* … */ }
#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn unmount(inst: i32) { /* … */ }
```

The bytes differ; the **interface** — and therefore phase-11 conformance — does not.
